bench.website: The artifact bench-out (table.md, table.json, samples.json) has no website table and no website sample (grep -c website: 0, 0, 0). pulse-api bench/budgets.json has no website entry. The run's failures belong to api, probe, status and notify. No A/B with bench/run.ts was run.

checklist.item: Queries. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for every query on the request path and at startup. Flag every full table scan (SCAN) and every temporary B-tree (USE TEMP B-TREE) over results.
checklist.evidence: The website is a static site with no database and no request path of its own. grep -rn "sqlite\|SELECT \|bun:sqlite\|createServer\|Bun.serve\|listen(" src scripts --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v test finds only src/build/static-server.ts:2,48,61, the local file server of the checks.

checklist.item: Startup. A CPU profile of the startup (bun --cpu-prof), with the top functions by self time.
checklist.evidence: The only process start is the build. bun cpu.ts: bun run build 1,054 ms CPU median of 5; bun scripts/build.ts 1,002 ms median of 10 (interleaved), 855 ms with NODE_ENV=production (byte-identical dist, diff -r exit 0). bun --cpu-prof --cpu-prof-interval=100 scripts/build.ts, 5 runs, exit 0: 3,779.1 ms sampled; top self time: marked setext-heading regex 713.2 ms (18.9 %), anonymous 180.5 ms (4.8 %), DateTimeFormat 102.0 ms (2.7 %), marked inline-text regex 100.7 ms (2.7 %), marked #e 88.9 ms (2.4 %), ReactElement react-jsx-runtime.development.js 80.8 ms (2.1 %). By file: native 49.1 %, marked.esm.js 17.3 %, react-dom-server-legacy.browser.development.js 14.3 %, react-jsx-runtime.development.js 3.5 %, esbuild main.js 2.0 %. Findings 2 and 4.

checklist.item: Costs that grow with data. The repository's bench, or a local A/B with a larger data set (for example 10x the bench seed). Report how each measured cost changes with the data size.
checklist.evidence: No website bench exists and the pulse-api bench has no website metric. timeout 600 bun growth.ts <copy> 1 10 (exit 0, median of 5): docs Markdown 415 KiB -> 4,149 KiB; one marked.lexer per file 47.1 -> 439.1 ms (9.3x); one renderMarkdown per file 97.0 -> 928.6 ms (9.6x); buildDocPages 196.2 -> 1,857.3 ms (9.5x); renderSite 79.5 -> 185.5 ms (2.3x); HTML written 929 -> 5,688 KiB; largest page gzip 15,066 -> 116,483 B; pages over the 60,000 B HTML budget 0 -> 4. All linear; buildDocPages costs 2x one render at every size (finding 4). The docs sidebar holds all 39 links on each docs page (2,903 B raw; all nav blocks 852 B gzip of 6,228 B). The canvas network is capped at 14 + 40 nodes (src/lib/network.ts:96-97).

checklist.item: Memory over time. RSS after N minutes of steady load, against the RSS at the start. Name N and the load.
checklist.evidence: N = 5 minutes. Load: Home open and visible in headless Chrome 156 at 1280x800 with animations on (network canvas about 30 fps, live preview 1 Hz). timeout 600 bun memrun.ts <copy> / 5 30 no-preference, exit 0, 11 samples. Renderer PSS 159.3 -> 148.6 MiB (-6.7 %), all Chrome PSS 415.0 -> 401.5 MiB, JS heap 1.07 -> 1.44 MiB (0.98-1.64 sawtooth), DOM nodes 908 and listeners 12 constant: no leak. CPU 10.0 % of one core over 300 s (renderer 5.1 %, GPU 4.9 %); 0.3 % with reduced motion and 0.3 % on /docs/api/rest-api/ (60 s each); 10.1 % (Home) and 11.0 % (Hosted) when scrolled to the end (60 s each). Finding 1.

checklist.item: Tests. CPU time per test file; name the slowest files.
checklist.evidence: bun run test: 195 pass, 0 fail, 30 files; CPU median 609 ms of 5 (605, 609, 618, 588, 609). Per file (bun test ./<file>, 3 runs): src/site.test.ts 289 ms, src/content/hosted.test.ts 200 ms, src/build/hover-scan.test.ts 199 ms, src/content/home.test.ts 198 ms, src/docs/page.test.ts 87 ms, src/build/static-server.test.ts 64 ms; the other 24 files 27-59 ms. The four slowest call loadSite() (esbuild of src/site.tsx, 70 ms CPU alone). Nine files exit 1 when run alone because of the 80 % coverage gate, with all tests passing. No test CPU budget exists for the website. Each run leaves 4 directories in .build/ (finding 5).

findings.title: The network canvas animation costs about 10 % of a CPU core for as long as Home or Hosted is visible, wherever the reader has scrolled to
findings.command: timeout 600 bun memrun.ts <copy> / 5 30 no-preference (headless Chrome 156, 1280x800; PSS and CPU of every Chrome process from /proc, CDP Performance.getMetrics); 60 s repeats: SCROLL=1 on / and /hosted/, motion reduce on /, and /docs/api/rest-api/
findings.excerpt:
CPU over 300 s: renderer 5.1 %, gpu 4.9 %, all chrome 10.0 % of one core; page task time 3.1 %
scrolled to y=5778 (Home): all chrome 10.1 %; scrolled to y=3546 (Hosted): all chrome 11.0 %
Home, reduce: all chrome 0.3 %; /docs/api/rest-api/: all chrome 0.3 %
findings.unit: % of one CPU core (all Chrome processes), Home open and visible
findings.repetitions: 1 run of 300 s with 11 samples; 60 s repeats on Home and Hosted scrolled to the end (10.1 %, 11.0 %)
findings.baseline: 0.3 % with reduced motion on the same page (60 s), 0.3 % on a docs page without the canvas (60 s)
findings.budget: none: the website has no runtime CPU budget, and pulse-api bench/budgets.json has no website entry
findings.detail: The canvas is position: fixed with inset: 0 (src/styles/components.css:397-404), so the IntersectionObserver (src/islands/network-canvas.ts:146-149) never reports it off screen. The loop runs at about 30 fps until the tab is hidden, and each frame redraws the whole static network (drawNetwork() at :106) before the pulses. The GPU share depends on the machine: headless Chrome renders with a software GPU here.
findings.fixDirection: Draw the static network once (a second canvas or a cached bitmap) and redraw only the pulses per frame; or stop the loop once the hero is out of view, or after some time.

findings.command: bun cpu.ts <copy> 2 <label> -- bun scripts/build.ts, alternated 5 times with -- env NODE_ENV=production bun scripts/build.ts (10 runs per side); diff -r dist-dev dist-prod; bun --cpu-prof --cpu-prof-interval=100 scripts/build.ts (5 runs) summed with prof.ts
findings.excerpt:
default: 971, 1004, 1031, 1037, 1042, 978, 1050, 1000, 994, 953 ms
NODE_ENV=production: 807, 817, 845, 856, 857, 828, 859, 867, 894, 854 ms
diff_exit=0
profile by file: react-dom-server-legacy.browser.development.js 14.3 %, react-jsx-runtime.development.js 3.5 % (validateProperties$2, validateProperty, warnUnknownProperties)
findings.unit: ms CPU per build (bun scripts/build.ts, warm docs cache)
findings.baseline: 855 ms with NODE_ENV=production (median of 10): -147 ms, -14.7 %, identical dist/
findings.budget: none: the website has no build CPU budget, and pulse-api bench/budgets.json has no website entry
findings.detail: load-site.ts compiles src/site.tsx with packages: "external" and no NODE_ENV, so react-dom/server and react/jsx-runtime resolve to their development builds. The islands already get define process.env.NODE_ENV = "production" (src/build/assets.ts:76).
findings.fixDirection: Set NODE_ENV=production for the server render of the build (in scripts/build.ts, or a build-only define in load-site.ts), so the tests can keep React's development checks.

findings.title: The web-font swap delays Home's LCP by about 0.6 s on simulated mobile and causes the only layout shifts of Home and Hosted; the fallback faces are not matched to the fonts
findings.command: lighthouse <origin>/ and <origin>/hosted/ --only-categories=performance --output=json --chrome-flags="--headless=new --no-sandbox" (Lighthouse 13.6.0, Chrome 156), mobile behind gzip, 3 runs with fonts and 3 with --blocked-url-patterns='*.woff2'; also --preset=desktop and the repository's plain static server, 3 runs each
findings.excerpt:
Home mobile LCP 1809, 1808, 1811 ms (fonts) vs 1235, 1205, 1209 ms (fonts blocked)
LCP element: p.t-lead (fonts) vs h1.t-display (fonts blocked)
Hosted mobile CLS 0.033, 0.033, 0.033 (fonts) vs 0, 0, 0 (fonts blocked); Home desktop CLS 0.053, 0.053, 0.000
layout-shifts: span.t-accent (Hosted), div.hero-side (Home desktop), cause "Web font loaded"
observed: fonts end 76-78 ms, FCP 81-83 ms, LCP 123-133 ms
findings.unit: ms LCP, Home, Lighthouse mobile (simulated), gzip server; CLS 0.033 (Hosted mobile) and 0.053 (Home desktop)
findings.baseline: the same pages with the fonts blocked: Home LCP 1,209 ms, CLS 0 on both pages; on the uncompressed repository server Home LCP is 2,256 ms
findings.budget: none in budget.json; Core Web Vitals 'good' limits LCP 2.5 s and CLS 0.1, which all medians pass
findings.detail: The fallbacks are local("Arial") and local("Courier New") with size-adjust: 100% only, no ascent, descent or line-gap override; no font is preloaded (grep -rn preload src finds nothing). The runner has no Arial or Courier New (fc-list | grep -i -E "arial|courier" is empty), so the shift size depends on the reader's system fonts.
findings.fixDirection: Give the fallback faces metric overrides (ascent-override, descent-override, line-gap-override and a measured size-adjust) for the fonts they replace, and consider preloading the Space Grotesk file used by the hero text.

  marked.lexer once per source      47.1 ms
  renderMarkdown once per source    97.0 ms
  buildDocPages (as the build)      196.2 ms
scale 10x: 39 sources, 4149 KiB Markdown
  marked.lexer once per source      439.1 ms
  renderMarkdown once per source    928.6 ms
  buildDocPages (as the build)      1857.3 ms

findings.command: rm -rf .build; for i in 1 2 3; do bun run test; ls .build | wc -l; du -sk .build; done
findings.excerpt:
exit=0 after run 1: 4 dirs, 340 KiB
exit=0 after run 2: 8 dirs, 676 KiB
exit=0 after run 3: 12 dirs, 1012 KiB
findings.unit: KiB of .build/ per bun run test (4 directories)
findings.baseline: 0 after bun run build, which clears .build/ (scripts/build.ts:47)
findings.detail: loadSite() makes mkdtemp(.build/site-) and never removes it; four test files call it (src/site.test.ts:47, src/content/home.test.ts:8, src/content/hosted.test.ts:7, src/build/hover-scan.test.ts:48). Developer disk only; it does not affect the site.

notes: Fonts are 78.7 % of Home's transfer behind gzip (106,166 of 134,945 B). The italic JetBrains Mono (43,134 B) serves only the .t-accent words of the hero headings (src/styles/tokens.css:256-262). budget.json limits font files per family, not font bytes.

The repository's static server (src/build/static-server.ts) sends no compression and no cache headers. It serves only the checks, but Lighthouse with it overstates the transfer: Home 195,937 B plain against 134,945 B with gzip, mobile LCP 2,256 against 1,809 ms. No host is chosen yet (site.config.ts).
The docs sidebar repeats all 39 links on every docs page (2,903 B raw; all nav blocks 852 B gzip of a 6,228 B gzip page). This grows linearly with the page count and is far from the HTML budget.
formatUpdated (src/docs/page.ts:77-80) builds a new Intl.DateTimeFormat per docs page: 102.0 ms self time over 5 profiled builds, about 20 ms per build.

Run alone, nine test files exit 1 with all tests passing, because the 80 % coverage gate of bunfig.toml applies to each single-file run (src/site.test.ts: 2 pass, 0 fail, 76.86 % lines, exit 1; exit 0 with a copy of bunfig.toml without coverageThreshold); this changes the exit code of the one-file command in the AGENTS.md table.

The pulse-api nightly bench does not measure the website. Build, test or Lighthouse budgets for the website would have to be added to pulse-api bench/budgets.json or the website's budget.json; that is a decision for the owner.

Measurement limits: resourceUsage() may miss the CPU of the esbuild service process, which is not a waited child. Headless Chrome renders with a software GPU, so the GPU share in finding 1 depends on the machine.
